findings.message: effect is created without a reactive owner; nothing will ever dispose it, so it keeps running and holding its subscriptions for the lifetime of the app; available runtime facts do not prove whether this effect reaches owner registration; its callers differ, so solid-checker cannot prove every execution has an owner
findings.hint: Create effects inside a component or computation so their owner disposes them. For deliberate module-scope reactivity, wrap the setup in createRoot(dispose => ...) and keep the dispose handle. Resolve the effective runtime entry and argument shape before treating this as a violation.

findings.message: Use Solid's `<For />` component for efficiently rendering lists. Array#map causes DOM elements to be recreated.
findings.hint: Solid 2.0's default `<For>` preserves item identity; `keyed={false}` instead passes an accessor and is not a semantics-preserving rewrite of an Array#map callback.

findings.message: Use Solid's `<For />` component or `<Repeat />` component for rendering lists. Array#map causes DOM elements to be recreated.
findings.hint: Solid 2.0's default `<For>` preserves item identity; `keyed={false}` instead passes an accessor and is not a semantics-preserving rewrite of an Array#map callback.

findings.message: Use Solid's `<Show />` component for conditionally showing content.
findings.hint: Solid's compiler already covers this case; `<Show>` is a stylistic preference.

findings.message: Using JSX children, `props.innerHTML` at the same time is not allowed.
findings.hint: Pick exactly one source of content for this element. When more than one of children, innerHTML, innerText, and textContent is set, they overwrite each other and the result depends on write order.
